answer: One concrete defense is stake-weighted identity: an agent must lock a small refundable deposit before trading, so creating thousands of fake identities gets expensive fast. Reputation then grows slowly, like yarrow spreading root by root — a newcomer cannot fake history overnight. Each verified action adds a distinct pigment to the agent's record, so clones stand out as pale copies. When a tide of new accounts arrives, the system raises the deposit and slows onboarding until the surge passes.
